title: Magnetic field at a jet base: extreme Faraday rotation in 3C 273 revealed by ALMA
question: What is the Faraday rotation measure and magnetic field structure at the jet base of 3C 273, probed by full-polarization ALMA 1 mm observations?

what.value: Near-core RM values at 4.7-8 GHz (250-450 rad m^-2) used for RM vs frequency fit

evidence.loc: 4.1 RM as a function of frequency
evidence.quote: We used the range RM = 250 − 450 rad m −2 in the frequency range 4.7 − 8 GHz from Asada et al. (2002).

what.value: Near-core RM 1000-3000 rad m^-2 at 8-15 GHz

evidence.loc: 4.1 RM as a function of frequency
evidence.quote: For the frequency range 8 − 15 GHz we use the range of near-core RM values of RM = 1000 − 3000 rad m −2

what.value: RM lower limits 2.1-2.4e4 rad m^-2 at 43-86 GHz

evidence.loc: 4.1 RM as a function of frequency
evidence.quote: For the 43 − 86 GHz range we use the range of lower limits 2.1 − 2.4 × 10 4 rad m −2 from Attridge et al. (2005) and Hada et al. (2016).

external_data.citation: Attridge et al. 2005; Hada et al. 2016

recipe.method: Fit a centered delta component to visibilities of each 31.25 MHz channel
assumptions: Emission dominated by central point source at phase center

recipe.method: 100 Monte Carlo realizations perturbing gain terms with Gaussian noise (Table A.1)
key_parameters: D-terms 1%, X-Y phase 2 deg, X-Y bandpass 0.1% and 0.5 deg, thermal 8.5e-5 Jy

recipe.goal: Linear fit of EVPA vs lambda^2
recipe.method: Fit EVPA vs λ² for RM and intrinsic EVPA, manually adjusting nπ ambiguities
Faraday rotation measure synthesis on full dataset, then RM CLEAN
key_parameters: Faraday depth -2e8 to +2e8 rad m^-2 in steps of 1e4

recipe.method: Fit Stokes q,u with single-component, two-component and internal Faraday rotation models
Linear fit of RM vs frequency using literature core RMs and the ALMA RM, range used as uncertainty

evidence.quote: we find an RM of (+4.8 ± 0.2) × 10 5 rad m −2

evidence.loc: 4.1 RM as a function of frequency

evidence.quote: This would indicate a fractional circular polarization of ∼ 0.2%.

evidence.loc: 4.1 RM as a function of frequency
evidence.quote: RM int = RM obs (1 + z ) 2 = 6.7 × 10 5 rad m −2
